# Sortify Offline download organization for rooted Android. Sortify moves eligible files into categories, preserves naming conflicts, identifies duplicates by contents, and records moves for Preview and Undo. **Version 5.0** adds Preview, custom rules, content-based duplicate detection, move history and Undo. Author: xCaptaiN09. MIT license. [Download v5.0](https://github.com/xCaptaiN09/Sortify/releases/tag/v5.0) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) ## Screenshots Actual captures from the Android WebUI. Select a screenshot to view it full size.

Home · Preview · History

Sorting results and category controls

## Defaults | Setting | Fresh installation | | --- | --- | | Automatic sorting | Off; enable it in Settings | | Automatic interval | One hour | | Keep recent downloads | One day; can be turned off | | Source | `/sdcard/Download` | | Destination | `/sdcard/Sortify` | | Unknown files | Others; can be left in Downloads instead | | History retention | 30 days, configurable from 1 to 365; latest 200 runs maximum | Manual sorting works when automatic sorting is off. Sort Now and the module manager's Action button both honor the delay, unfinished-download checks, ignore rules, disabled categories and Undo protection. They start a run immediately; they do not force every file to move. Compatible settings are retained on upgrade. A v4 installation migrates its existing interval and automatic sorting behavior. The new one-day delay starts enabled; review it in Settings after upgrading. Existing organized files are never rearranged as part of installation. ## Categories and rules Documents, Images, Videos, Audio, Archives, Apps and Others are available by default. Ebooks, Fonts, Subtitles, Code/config and Torrents are optional presets. Advanced settings allow custom categories, extensions, destination folders, filename/glob rules, priority ordering and ignore patterns. - Custom rules are evaluated in visible order, followed by extension mappings. - When rules overlap, Preview identifies the matching rules and winner. - A disabled category leaves matching files in the source; it does not reroute them into Others or Duplicates. - Unknown extensions use Others unless the user selects Leave in Downloads. - Only files directly inside the source are scanned; subfolders are untouched. - Destinations must be separate from the source and within the configured shared storage root. System/module/state paths and overlapping source/output trees are rejected. Changing a category does not move its previously organized files. ## Duplicates and file preservation A filename match is not proof of a duplicate. Sortify first compares sizes, then SHA-256 and bytes. An identical incoming copy goes to Duplicates; the organized copy stays in place. Different contents sharing a name remain in the normal category under an available name, such as `report (1).pdf`. Every destination is created exclusively. Repeated collisions inside Duplicates also receive available names. Sortify does not automatically delete duplicate copies. Transfers are copied, verified and recorded before removing the source; interrupted operations are reconciled from a persistent journal. Source capture requires Linux renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE; unsupported filesystems fail without replacing another file. Android shared-storage directory modes are not assumed to make staging folders private. Interrupted uncertain copies are preserved and flagged for inspection rather than automatically deleted. ## Download handling Hidden files and recognized temporary suffixes are skipped. Normally named files must have an unchanged identity/size/modification time across observations and a minimum stability period before moving. They are checked again around comparison and transfer. The optional one-day delay is separate from stability checks. With the one-day delay enabled, both the file's modification time and its unchanged observation period must be at least 24 hours old. An existing old file can therefore wait another day after Sortify first sees it. Turning the delay off removes that day-long wait; the minimum 60-second stability check remains. If a run shows **0 moved** and only skipped files, open Preview or the run in History to read each reason. For immediate testing, disable **Keep recent downloads for 1 day** in Settings, save, then use Preview and Sort Now. Automatic sorting can remain off while testing manual sorting. Where readable, process file descriptors and shared writable mappings provide an additional active-writer check. Android SELinux/procfs restrictions can hide other processes; no writer result is treated as proof of completion. A paused download can look stable. Not all download apps expose a completion signal, so these checks cannot prove completion for every app. The one-day delay uses available file modification times and stability observations rather than claiming an exact universal download-completion timestamp. ## Installation Download **Sortify-v5.0.zip** from the release assets, install it through your module manager and reboot. GitHub's generated source archives do not contain the compiled helpers and are not installable modules. The installer preserves existing settings, prints a short setup status and keeps only the helper for your device. If settings setup fails, its diagnostic output is saved in `/data/adb/sortify/install.log`; successful setup removes that temporary log. ## WebUI and Action Open the module's WebUI in a compatible KernelSU-family manager: - **Home:** actual run state, last result, automatic sorting toggle, Preview, Sort Now and Stop. - **Preview:** planned destinations, naming changes, duplicate matches, rule matches and reasons for skipped files. Preview never moves files. - **History:** per-file and whole-run Undo, results and conflicts. - **Settings:** scheduling, delay, folders, categories, rules, exclusions, retention and export/import. The interface uses one light editorial theme: a fading top gradient, open sections, fine dividers, line artwork and locally bundled Bodoni Moda/DM Sans fonts. There is no appearance selector or dependency on a device theme. The UI uses the KernelSU callback execution bridge. A regular browser cannot access device storage; `?demo=1` enables an explicitly labeled, isolated demo. The bundled classic script also supports opening `webroot/index.html` directly for local preview. Append `?demo=1` to that file URL to explore sample data. Without a manager bridge, normal mode reports that device access is unavailable and disables file-changing controls. The built-in module manager Action button remains available independently of the WebUI. Magisk does not gain a built-in WebUI merely by installing this module; only claim compatibility with a particular external WebUI host after testing it. Stop finishes the current file and stops before the next. It does not disable future automatic runs. All sorting and Undo entry points share a process lock. Another request while busy reports Already running. ## Undo, retention and settings Undo restores unchanged moved files only when their original paths are free. Conflicts leave the files intact. Whole-run Undo reports partial results. Restored files receive persistent holds so the next run cannot immediately move them back. Release those holds in **History → Kept in place** when ready to sort them again. History keeps at most the latest 200 runs and removes records older than your configured retention period. History retention/clearing removes Undo records, not organized files. Undo holds survive history clearing. Export/import contains settings and rules, not process state or move history; imported settings are validated before being applied. ## Removal Remove/disable the module through its manager. The daemon observes the module's lifecycle flags and finishes the current file before exiting. Organized files and `/data/adb/sortify` settings/history remain preserved. No broad process-name kill or deletion of user files is performed. ## Build and verify Before packaging WebUI source changes, run `npm ci` and `npm run build:web`. The checked-in `webroot/app.js` is generated from the modular sources. Development needs Go 1.24+, Python 3.10+ and Node 20+. None of these runtimes is required on the phone. The native helper uses only the Go standard library. ```sh npm ci npm run build:web cd core go test -race ./... cd .. node --test tests/webui.test.mjs python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v python3 tools/build.py python3 tools/package.py ``` Use `python3 tools/build.py --go /path/to/go` if Go is not on PATH. Output: `dist/Sortify-v5.0.zip`. CI builds a module ZIP as a downloadable artifact; it does not publish a release or advance the update feed. ARM64 is built for Android as PIE. ARMv7, x86 and x86_64 use static Linux helper builds without an external interpreter. Architecture builds and host tests are not substitutes for device testing. See `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md` for the actual verification results and outstanding checks. For an isolated desktop backend fixture, build with `--host-only`, then run: ```sh build/bin/host/sortify --state /tmp/sortify-state --storage /tmp/sortify-storage --module "$PWD" init ``` Use temporary directories outside one another. Never point a development test at real downloads. Requests support base64 JSON and a request-file/stdin interface; the WebUI uses only the fixed wrapper and encoded data, not constructed commands containing filenames. ## Update identity The module ID remains `sortify`. Version 5.0 uses `versionCode=11`, increased from v4.0's code 10. The manager checks `update.json` for the matching release ZIP and changelog. Future releases must keep the module ID and increase the version code. [Requirements](docs/NEXT_UPDATE.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

Sortify

Offline download organization for rooted Android. Sortify moves eligible files

into categories, preserves naming conflicts, identifies duplicates by contents,

and records moves for Preview and Undo.

Version 5.0 adds Preview, custom rules, content-based duplicate detection,

move history and Undo. Author: xCaptaiN09. MIT license.

Download v5.0 ·

Changelog

Screenshots

Actual captures from the Android WebUI. Select a screenshot to view it full size.

Home · Preview · History

Sorting results and category controls

Defaults

| Setting | Fresh installation |

| --- | --- |

| Automatic sorting | Off; enable it in Settings |

| Automatic interval | One hour |

| Keep recent downloads | One day; can be turned off |

| Source | /sdcard/Download |

| Destination | /sdcard/Sortify |

| Unknown files | Others; can be left in Downloads instead |

| History retention | 30 days, configurable from 1 to 365; latest 200 runs maximum |

Manual sorting works when automatic sorting is off. Sort Now and the module

manager's Action button both honor the delay, unfinished-download checks, ignore

rules, disabled categories and Undo protection. They start a run immediately;

they do not force every file to move.

Compatible settings are retained on upgrade. A v4 installation migrates its

existing interval and automatic sorting behavior. The new one-day delay starts

enabled; review it in Settings after upgrading. Existing organized files are

never rearranged as part of installation.

Categories and rules

Documents, Images, Videos, Audio, Archives, Apps and Others are available by

default. Ebooks, Fonts, Subtitles, Code/config and Torrents are optional presets.

Advanced settings allow custom categories, extensions, destination folders,

filename/glob rules, priority ordering and ignore patterns.

  • Custom rules are evaluated in visible order, followed by extension mappings.
  • When rules overlap, Preview identifies the matching rules and winner.
  • A disabled category leaves matching files in the source; it does not reroute

    • them into Others or Duplicates.

  • Unknown extensions use Others unless the user selects Leave in Downloads.
  • Only files directly inside the source are scanned; subfolders are untouched.
  • Destinations must be separate from the source and within the configured shared

    • storage root. System/module/state paths and overlapping source/output trees

    are rejected. Changing a category does not move its previously organized files.

    Duplicates and file preservation

    A filename match is not proof of a duplicate. Sortify first compares sizes, then

    SHA-256 and bytes. An identical incoming copy goes to Duplicates; the organized

    copy stays in place. Different contents sharing a name remain in the normal

    category under an available name, such as report (1).pdf.

    Every destination is created exclusively. Repeated collisions inside Duplicates

    also receive available names. Sortify does not automatically delete duplicate

    copies. Transfers are copied, verified and recorded before removing the source;

    interrupted operations are reconciled from a persistent journal. Source capture

    requires Linux renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE; unsupported filesystems fail

    without replacing another file. Android shared-storage directory modes are not

    assumed to make staging folders private. Interrupted uncertain copies are

    preserved and flagged for inspection rather than automatically deleted.

    Download handling

    Hidden files and recognized temporary suffixes are skipped. Normally named files

    must have an unchanged identity/size/modification time across observations and a

    minimum stability period before moving. They are checked again around comparison

    and transfer. The optional one-day delay is separate from stability checks.

    With the one-day delay enabled, both the file's modification time and its

    unchanged observation period must be at least 24 hours old. An existing old file

    can therefore wait another day after Sortify first sees it. Turning the delay

    off removes that day-long wait; the minimum 60-second stability check remains.

    If a run shows 0 moved and only skipped files, open Preview or the run in

    History to read each reason. For immediate testing, disable **Keep recent

    downloads for 1 day** in Settings, save, then use Preview and Sort Now. Automatic

    sorting can remain off while testing manual sorting.

    Where readable, process file descriptors and shared writable mappings provide

    an additional active-writer check. Android SELinux/procfs restrictions can hide

    other processes; no writer result is treated as proof of completion.

    A paused download can look stable. Not all download apps expose a completion

    signal, so these checks cannot prove completion for every app. The one-day delay

    uses available file modification times and stability observations rather than

    claiming an exact universal download-completion timestamp.

    Installation

    Download Sortify-v5.0.zip from the release assets, install it through your

    module manager and reboot. GitHub's generated source archives do not contain the

    compiled helpers and are not installable modules. The installer preserves existing

    settings, prints a short setup status and keeps only the helper for your device.

    If settings setup fails, its diagnostic output is saved in

    /data/adb/sortify/install.log; successful setup removes that temporary log.

    WebUI and Action

    Open the module's WebUI in a compatible KernelSU-family manager:

  • **Home:** actual run state, last result, automatic sorting toggle, Preview,

    • Sort Now and Stop.

  • **Preview:** planned destinations, naming changes, duplicate matches, rule

    • matches and reasons for skipped files. Preview never moves files.

  • **History:** per-file and whole-run Undo, results and conflicts.
  • **Settings:** scheduling, delay, folders, categories, rules, exclusions,

    • retention and export/import.

    The interface uses one light editorial theme: a fading top gradient, open

    sections, fine dividers, line artwork and locally bundled Bodoni Moda/DM Sans

    fonts. There is no appearance selector or dependency on a device theme.

    The UI uses the KernelSU callback execution bridge. A regular browser cannot

    access device storage; ?demo=1 enables an explicitly labeled, isolated demo.

    The bundled classic script also supports opening webroot/index.html directly

    for local preview. Append ?demo=1 to that file URL to explore sample data.

    Without a manager bridge, normal mode reports that device access is unavailable

    and disables file-changing controls.

    The built-in module manager Action button remains available independently of the

    WebUI. Magisk does not gain a built-in WebUI merely by installing this module;

    only claim compatibility with a particular external WebUI host after testing it.

    Stop finishes the current file and stops before the next. It does not disable

    future automatic runs. All sorting and Undo entry points share a process lock.

    Another request while busy reports Already running.

    Undo, retention and settings

    Undo restores unchanged moved files only when their original paths are free.

    Conflicts leave the files intact. Whole-run Undo reports partial results.

    Restored files receive persistent holds so the next run cannot immediately move

    them back. Release those holds in History → Kept in place when ready to sort

    them again.

    History keeps at most the latest 200 runs and removes records older than your

    configured retention period. History retention/clearing removes Undo records,

    not organized files. Undo holds

    survive history clearing. Export/import contains settings and rules, not process

    state or move history; imported settings are validated before being applied.

    Removal

    Remove/disable the module through its manager. The daemon observes the module's

    lifecycle flags and finishes the current file before exiting. Organized files and

    /data/adb/sortify settings/history remain preserved. No broad process-name kill

    or deletion of user files is performed.

    Build and verify

    Before packaging WebUI source changes, run npm ci and npm run build:web.

    The checked-in webroot/app.js is generated from the modular sources.

    Development needs Go 1.24+, Python 3.10+ and Node 20+. None of these runtimes is

    required on the phone. The native helper uses only the Go standard library.

    npm ci
npm run build:web
cd core
go test -race ./...
cd ..
node --test tests/webui.test.mjs
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
python3 tools/build.py
python3 tools/package.py

    Use python3 tools/build.py --go /path/to/go if Go is not on PATH. Output:

    dist/Sortify-v5.0.zip. CI builds a module ZIP as a downloadable artifact;

    it does not publish a release or advance the update feed.

    ARM64 is built for Android as PIE. ARMv7, x86 and x86_64 use static Linux helper

    builds without an external interpreter. Architecture builds and host tests are

    not substitutes for device testing. See docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md for the

    actual verification results and outstanding checks.

    For an isolated desktop backend fixture, build with --host-only, then run:

    build/bin/host/sortify --state /tmp/sortify-state --storage /tmp/sortify-storage --module "$PWD" init

    Use temporary directories outside one another. Never point a development test at

    real downloads. Requests support base64 JSON and a request-file/stdin interface;

    the WebUI uses only the fixed wrapper and encoded data, not constructed commands

    containing filenames.

    Update identity

    The module ID remains sortify. Version 5.0 uses versionCode=11, increased from

    v4.0's code 10. The manager checks update.json for the matching release ZIP and

    changelog. Future releases must keep the module ID and increase the version code.

    Requirements · Changelog
